thread:
jana: Quick question for SDK folks — thinking about consolidating the call shape across Python/TS/Go. Main constraints: ergonomic sync/async, clear transport fallback (grpc/http/ws), and consistent retry semantics for pagination/streaming. Any preferences or strong 🚫 on approaches? :thinking:

sam: +1 on a single core model. My take: core async primitives in each SDK, with language-idiomatic thin wrappers. For Python provide a sync wrapper, for TS promise-based top-level, for Go explicit contexts. Keep the transport layer pluggable.

liam: Agreed. Also +1 to prefer gRPC internally (dedicated/private) for perf, use HTTP/1.1+ chunked or SSE for hosted public browser flows. WebSockets only if we need bi-directional.

maria: Two quick asks: 1) pagination resume tokens must be opaque (server-owned) so we can change internals, 2) retries for paged endpoints need to consider partial page semantics (don't double-apply side effects).

sam: Right — for retries we should define two modes: idempotent (safe to retry) and resumeable (has continuation token). Implementation idea: attach an explicit "continuation_token" in responses; clients retry by replaying up to the last confirmed continuation token.

jana: What about streaming (chat/generation) vs paginated generation? Should we have a single API that multiplexes both or separate call shapes?

liam: Separate. Streaming needs different backpressure, resume semantics, and often uses a streaming transport (SSE/ws/grpc-stream). Paged calls are unary + token. Trying to merge them makes client code awkward.

sam: For Python ergonomics: core async API + a sync helper is easiest to maintain. Example pattern (small):
```python
# async core
async def generate_async(prompt):
    async with client.stream_generate(prompt) as s:
        async for chunk in s:
            yield chunk

# sync wrapper
def generate(prompt):
    return list(asyncio.run(generate_async(prompt)))
```
This keeps a single codepath and minimal surface.

maria: For TS: promise-based + an AsyncIterable for streaming seems natural (async iterators are already good). For browsers that can't speak gRPC, we should implement an HTTP chunking fallback that maps to the same AsyncIterable shape.

jana: Good. A couple of policy-level decisions we need:
- transport preference order (grpc -> http2 -> http1 chunking)
- default retry policy + idempotency markers (client-visible header?)
- whether to expose resume tokens as first-class or hide behind client helpers

liam: Proposal: transport preference order per deployment tier: Dedicated/Private: grpc (or grpc-web for browser); Hosted: http1 chunking + explicit SSE; allow explicit override in client config.

sam: For retry policy, expose a named policy ("strict", "conservative", "none") and a per-call option. Idempotency keys should be optional but recommended for mutating calls. For pagination, prefer resume tokens over naive retries.

maria: I'd push to surface resume tokens as a helper API: e.g., client.fetch_page(..., resume_from=token) and also client.get_resume_helper() which returns a small object that knows how to rehydrate. Keep token string opaque but easy to pass around.

devex-bot: reminder: please open an SDK API RFC issue with the concrete examples for Py/TS/Go and attach compatibility matrix. Tag @sam @maria @liam.

jana: Action items: sam to sketch Python wrapper pattern (+ perf notes), maria to prototype TS AsyncIterable + http-chunk fallback, liam to write transport preference matrix (grpc/http/ws by tier). I'll collect and file the RFC early next week. :+1:

sam: ack. I'll post a short Gist with the sync-wrapper pattern.

maria: ack, I'll try a tiny browser PoC with fetch() + ReadableStream mapping to AsyncIterator.

liam: will draft matrix. One more note — we should standardize a small set of client errors for 'resume not supported' vs 'token invalid' so higher layers can handle uniformly.

jana: Great. Thanks all — ping me if you want to pair on the RFC text.
